category_title: Low-attaining students developing fraction concepts through physical measurement with manipulatives
minimal_context: The student is using red and brown Cuisenaire rods to determine fraction names during a mathematics lesson.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please use these red and brown Cuisenaire rods to work on your fractions.

STUDENT: (Places the red rods beside the brown rod) What it is. I'm kind of measuring it.

TUTOR: What are you trying to measure?

STUDENT: See if it's a quarter or not. Because I went like this... (moves small red rods along the longer rod).

TUTOR: How would you know if it is a quarter?

STUDENT: An ordinary guess. I was happy because that was pretty easy until I got up to number 6, 'cause I knew it all. Now I need you to tell me the parts.

options.A: Implement a self-management intervention during the fraction lesson, involving self-monitoring, self-evaluation, and self-reinforcement using a daily checklist for the mathematics tasks.
options.B: Maintain a ratio of praise to correction at 3:1 or 4:1 during the fraction lesson, applying this consistently throughout the mathematics session.
options.C: Use desk carrels during the fraction lesson to provide personal space and make a clear distinction between individual and group mathematics activity areas.
options.D: Conduct scaffolding conversations in chunks over the course of the fraction lesson, coming and going then resuming the next part of the interlinked conversation.
